keyFindings.description: The related_checks record retry runs on its own sync.WaitGroup (relatedRecordRetries) next to main's backgroundWork, which #2449 brought in this merge. backgroundWork exists because work may start while wait is already waiting (server.go:430-433): cmd/dispatch/shutdown.go calls waitBackground once httpDrainBeforeDocuments has passed with requests still in flight. A late unkeyed create (a script, the daemon outbox) whose first record attempt fails can then call relatedRecordRetries.Go after Wait began from zero, which sync.WaitGroup forbids and which can panic in the window where Wait is releasing; otherwise the retry runs after waitBackground returned. Fix: run the retry with s.detached.goDetached, and delete the relatedRecordRetries field, its Wait at server.go:427 and the related-check clauses in the Register and waitBackground comments. Keep relatedRecordRetrying, which enforces the retry limit.

The allowlist reason says the rows are written after the write marked its key, but respondWithExistingExternalIssue commits only a read, marks no key, and records an already_exists row. Say the row records the check whether or not the write wrote, and a duplicate after a takeover only adds one row of statistics.

'cancelled' is described as the request ending first. Under #2449 a keyed handler's context is detached from the client and ends only at keyedRunLimit, with no cause, so for a keyed write cancelled means the keyed run's own bound. Say so where cancelled is described.

verified.keyedLayer: A replayed create returns its stored status (request_keys.go:990), so the client's created (201) and already-held (200) stay right on a replay. Keyed handlers run on WithoutCancel(r.Context()) bounded by keyedRunLimit (10 min), so the 5 s allowance ends first and a slow check records timeout. POST /projects/{key}/related is keyed like every POST, as main keys its other read-only POSTs; it writes nothing and stores only its answer.
